records.title: The Living Canopy
records.text: On Kaelith, forests grow across cliffs and islands of floating stone. Selenari stories describe paths that open to a remembered song, springs that answer a promise, and ancient trees whose roots shelter whole communities. Visitors disagree about what is magic, what is craft and what remains unknown.

records.title: The Courts and the Commons
records.text: The first surviving accounts tell of forest courts, river settlements and wandering keepers who carried news between them. Their alliances were not always peaceful. After a long struggle over the water routes, several communities began meeting beneath a great root bridge to settle disputes and share access to the springs.

records.title: Beyond the Canopy
records.text: Selenari navigators eventually followed lights above the highest floating islands and learned to cross between worlds. The Auroran Compact grew from agreements between their settlements and other peoples they met. It remains a compact of members rather than a single family or species.

records.title: A Question Left Open
records.text: The oldest song tablets contain a verse about a path that leads beyond the known sky. Some archivists consider it a map; others read it as a lesson about welcoming strangers. Both interpretations are preserved here, together with the voices that challenge them.

records.title: Letters from Meridian
records.text: During the Meridian storm, an Auroran guide wrote that her ship opened a safe route for a damaged Ravel convoy and helped direct it to a Frontier dock. Her letters praise the cooperation that followed, but omit the names of the passengers. Other accounts in this archive question whether the route was opened before or after the convoy sent its distress call.

archives.name: Vesper House of Voices
archives.world_type: Early coastal settlements and tidal plains

records.title: Before the Harbours
records.text: The earliest Tavren communities on Nareth lived along tidal plains, making tools from stone, shell and bone. Their technology was simple, but their lives were not: generations of navigators memorised the tides, mapped the stars in stories and taught one another where the sea could be crossed safely.

records.title: The Long Exchange
records.text: Coastal communities traded food, pigments and carved records, and they also fought over sheltered water. The first councils began as seasonal gatherings where rivals could negotiate safe passage. Their agreements changed over centuries as new towns and new voices joined them.

records.title: From Canoes to Starships
records.text: Later Tavren engineers built ocean vessels, observatories and, eventually, spacecraft. The Vesper Guild traces its name to night crossings between the old harbours. Today its merchants and surveyors come from many worlds, and membership depends on their agreements rather than ancestry.

records.title: The Unfinished Tide Song
records.text: Several communities remember different endings to the same ancient voyage. The House of Voices records each version beside the others. Its keepers argue that a shared past becomes richer when disagreements are kept in the record.

records.title: The Relief Ledger
records.text: A Vesper quartermaster recorded food, sealant and navigation charts supplied during the Meridian storm. The ledger lists some cargo as a gift and other cargo as a debt, with later entries disputing who had authority to promise repayment. Its figures do not agree with every account of the rescue.

records.title: A World of Pressure
records.text: Varkesh has dense, corrosive air, heavy gravity and volcanic basins. It is dangerous to many visiting species without protective equipment, but it is home to the Kethari. Their settlements grew around sheltered thermal channels where water and minerals could be gathered.

records.title: The Shelter Compacts
records.text: Early Kethari communities learned to reinforce caverns and share maintenance of the barriers that kept their homes safe. Records also describe bitter arguments over who controlled those shelters. The shelter compacts established shared obligations and the right to request aid during a breach.

records.title: Forges Among the Stars
records.text: Pressure engineering and careful recycling became foundations of Kethari industry. Spaceflight brought new resources and new political conflicts. The Ravel Concord formed through negotiated agreements among industrial settlements and neighbouring peoples, not through one uninterrupted story of progress.

records.title: The Sealed Chamber
records.text: A sealed chamber beneath an old basin bears marks from a people whose identity remains disputed. The Concord funds several competing investigations and keeps their findings available here. No single explanation has been accepted as final.

records.title: Testimony of the Breach
records.text: A Ravel engineer remembered the Meridian storm from inside a failing convoy ship. Her account describes the crew holding a pressure barrier while strangers negotiated where to dock. She credited help from several factions but argued that later histories treated the convoy members as helpless passengers rather than people who kept one another alive.

archives.name: Frontier Continuity Archive
archives.world_type: Futuristic orbital cities and habitat rings

records.title: The Ring Cities
records.text: Around Ilyra, generations of Ilyrans built inhabited rings, gardens and research cities. Biological people and machine intelligences shared many of those habitats. Their advanced systems could sustain vast populations, but decisions about ownership, autonomy and memory remained matters of disagreement.

records.title: The Departure
records.text: A series of political and ecological crises led some habitat communities to leave. Their reasons differed: some sought independence, others wanted room to rebuild, and many simply followed family. Their ships carried seed libraries, engineering records and accounts of mistakes they did not want forgotten.

records.title: The Free Frontier
records.text: Ilyran travellers joined settlements and ships from many other civilizations along the outer routes. The Free Frontier grew from local aid agreements among them. Its members include people who never lived near Ilyra and whose histories are preserved in their own right.

records.title: Copies and Continuity
records.text: Frontier archivists debate what it means for a person or a culture to continue when memories can be copied and habitats can be rebuilt. This station keeps technical records beside personal testimony, including accounts that reject the idea that every copy is the same person.

records.title: Open Dock Recording
records.text: A Frontier dockkeeper recorded the arrival of the damaged convoy after the Meridian storm. The recording includes unnamed travellers whose families do not appear in the later public agreement. Frontier archivists keep the full account beside the official histories so that those missing voices can still be sought.
